answer: Each identity must present a sequential state proof whose memory-hardness resists parallel evaluation and whose tenure is soulbound, so a farm cannot split one proof across a thousand machines and cannot hand the result to a fresh account. Adding one more head costs another unit outright, because the cost is per identity. The opal is the sequential proof, the signal the tenure it is bound to, and the dune the memory-hardness that resists parallel evaluation; the opal and the signal are per identity, and it is the dune that stops one proof serving a hundred clones.
